info:
In Portuguese, accents are written marks placed on vowels that show how the word should be pronounced. They can indicate which syllable is stressed, whether a vowel is open or closed, or if it is nasalized. Accents also help distinguish words that are spelled the same but have different meanings.

The main accents are:

Acute (´) → makes the vowel more open (á, é, ó). Example: avó (grandmother).

Circumflex (ˆ) → makes the vowel more closed (â, ê, ô). Example: avô (grandfather).

Tilde (~) → makes the vowel nasal (ão, ões). Example: pão (bread).

Grave (`) → shows a contraction (à = “to the”), and sometimes marks stress.

Accents are not optional in Portuguese: leaving them out can change the meaning of a word or make it hard to pronounce correctly
